exposure: Plasma eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) concentrations
cohort: The study included 376 women with early preterm birth (<34 gestational weeks) and 348 random control women from the Danish National Birth Cohort, excluding preeclampsia cases.
finding: Low plasma concentrations of EPA and DHA during pregnancy, particularly below 1.6%, were strongly associated with a significantly increased risk of early preterm birth.
